subject: Computer Networking
title: Li-Fi: Internet from Light
description: A micro-lesson that makes Li-Fi: Internet from Light usable.

hook.text: What if your ceiling light delivered internet? Li-Fi uses visible light instead of radio waves.

buildup.text: LEDs flicker billions of times per second — invisible to us. Photodetectors read the flickers as data.

discovery.text: Li-Fi hits 200+ Gbps in labs. The visible light spectrum is 10,000 times wider than radio.

twist.text: Light can't pass through walls. A limitation, but also a security feature: signals stay in the room.

climax.text: Li-Fi suits hospitals (no radio interference), aircraft, and secure rooms. It complements Wi-Fi.

punchline.text: Li-Fi turns light into data. Insanely fast and perfectly contained.

quiz.question: Why is Li-Fi considered more secure than Wi-Fi?
options: Light signals can't pass through walls, containing the signal to one room
It uses stronger encryption than any radio protocol
It requires a physical cable connection

details.summary: Li-Fi uses modulated LED light to transmit data wirelessly at speeds up to 10 Gbps. Light switches on and off billions of times per second, invisible to the human eye, encoding data in the flickering pattern. Li-Fi cannot penetrate walls, providing inherent security and zero radio interference.
details.whyItMatters: Li-Fi offers massive bandwidth in the visible light spectrum, which is 10,000 times wider than the radio spectrum. It enables high-speed connectivity in environments where radio frequency communication is restricted.
takeaways: LED lights modulate at billions of hertz to carry data
Speeds reach 10 Gbps with no radio frequency interference
Light cannot penetrate walls, providing physical security

faq.question: How does Li-Fi achieve high speeds?
faq.answer: Li-Fi modulates LED brightness at frequencies invisible to the eye. The visible light spectrum offers about 300 THz of bandwidth compared to the radio spectrum's limited GHz. Advanced modulation and MIMO techniques using multiple LEDs push practical speeds beyond 10 Gbps in laboratory settings.

faq.question: What are the limitations of Li-Fi?
faq.answer: Li-Fi requires line of sight and cannot pass through walls or opaque objects. Sunlight interference affects outdoor use. Coverage is limited to lit areas.
